chunks: What Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

He said: He was asked about a man who, when the sun declines while he is at home, then departs on a journey. He said: He begins with the zawal prayer and prays it, then prays al-ula (the zuhr) shortened to two rak'ahs, because he departed from his home before the time of al-ula arrived.

And he was asked: What if he departs after the time of al-ula has arrived? He said: He prays al-ula as four rak'ahs, then after it he prays the nawafil of eight rak'ahs, because he departed from his home after the time of al-ula had arrived. Then when the time of asr arrives, he prays asr with a shortening — and it is two rak'ahs — because he departed on the journey before the time of asr arrived.

key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: zawal — the moment the sun passes its zenith; here denotes the voluntary nawāfil prayers performed at that time
key_terms.النَّوَافِلِ: nawāfil — voluntary supererogatory prayers; specifically the 8-rakʿah cycle associated with zuhr
key_terms.الْأُولَى: al-ūlā — lit. 'the first'; classical Shia term for the zuhr (midday obligatory prayer)
key_terms.بِتَقْصِيرِ: taqṣīr — shortening (qasr); the legal reduction of four-rakʿah prayers to two while traveling

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about how a traveler should pray zuhr and asr when departing during or after the midday prayer time?
ai.summary: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq (AS) addresses a traveler who departs around the time of the midday prayer, distinguishing two scenarios: if he departs before the zuhr time becomes binding he prays it shortened (2 rakʿahs, no nawāfil); if he departs after, he prays it in full (4 rakʿahs) with the 8-rakʿah nawāfil, then prays ʿaṣr shortened as he is now a traveler.
